Harkesh Manuja J. (Oral)
1.
This common judgment of mine shall dispose of above mentioned five appeals as they all involve common question of law and facts.

For convenience, the facts are being taken from RFA-2708- 1998 (O&M).
2.

By way of present appeal, challenge has been laid to an award dated 22.01.1998 passed by the Reference Court, Kaithal whereby, the reference petition filed under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for brevity, "1894 Act") at the instance of appellant-landowner(s), seeking enhancement of compensation was partly accepted.

3. In the present case, notification under Section 4 of the 1894 Act was issued on 12.07.1993,
pertaining to proposed acquisition of land measuring 11.50 acres situated in village Chandana,
Hadbast No.18, Tehsil and District Kaithal for public purpose namely, for the construction of Dhundheri minor from R.D. 0 to 34750 off taking from RD 225950 Sirsa Branch.

4. Award No.4 dated 13.06.1995, under Section 11 of the 1894 Act was passed by the Land Acquisition Collector while making the assessment of market value of the acquired land @ Rs.1 lac per acre for Nehri land and Rs.90,000/- per acre for Chahi land.

5. Aggrieved thereof, the appellant(s)/landowner(s) filed 2 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:084367 RFA-2708-1998 (O&M) --3-- Chandan vs Haryana State on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34756690/
2 and other connected cases reference under Section 18 of the 1894 Act, seeking enhancement of compensation, besides claiming severance compensation in case of land owned by one Lal Chand forming part of the same notification.

6. The Reference Court vide award dated 22.01.1998 accepted the reference petition in part, making assessment of market value @ Rs.1 lakh per acre for Nehri land and @ Rs.90,000/- per acre for Chahi land, besides, awarding other statutory benefits under Section 23(1-A) read with Section 34 of the 1894 Act, however, neither statutory benefit of solatium was awarded in favour of the landowners nor any compensation on account of severance was awarded in favour of Lal Chand.
Hence, the present appeal(s).
7.

Impugning the aforesaid award, learned Senior counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant(s)
submits that the Reference Court went wrong while discarding the evidence in the shape of sale deeds (Ex.P1 and P-3) which belong to the same revenue estate i.e. village Chandana.

Learned Senior counsel further submits that the sale deed dated 04.10.1985 (Ex.P-1) pertains to 5 marlas of land sold for Rs.5000/- and the same should have been considered and appreciated after imposing suitable cut while making assessment of compensation by the Reference Court.

He also submits that in case of Lal Chand, bifurcation of his land on two sides of the minor was not disputed, and as such, suitable compensation on this account was required to be granted in his favour.
He further points out that the Reference Court went wrong while not specifying the grant of benefit of solatium in favour of landowners and thus, the award was required to be modified.
3 of 5

On the other hand, learned counsel representing the respondents-State submits that the sale deed (Ex.P-1), which was pertaining to a small piece of land measuring 5 marlas was rightly discarded by the Reference Court there being no similarity of it about the commercial potentiality with the land forming part of the acquisition.

He further submits that the impugned award passed by the Reference Court warrants no interference as regards declining of relief on account of severance charges in favour of Lal Chand for the reasons that the bridges were to be constructed on all the places wherever those were pre-existing on the old water course and thus, landowner-Lal Chand was not at loss on account of any bifurcation of land.
No possible/plausible objection could be raised on behalf of learned State counsel as regards the statutory benefit of solatium to be awarded in favour of the land owners.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the paper book.

10. In the present case, no merit can be found in the submissions made on behalf of the learned Senior counsel on the point of non- consideration of sale deed (Ex.P-1) by the Reference Court as the same pertains to a small piece of land measuring 5 marlas and that too, when its locational position/commercial potentiality has not been got compared by the appellants-landowners with the land under acquisition by proving any aks shajra or site plan.
11.

Further, there is substance in the submissions made on behalf of the appellants-landowners as regards non-grant of statutory benefit of solatium in favour of the appellants-landowners in terms of Section 23(2) of 4 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:084367 RFA-2708-1998 (O&M) --5-- and other connected cases the 1894 Act, which essentially was required to be awarded to the appellants/land-owners on account of acquisition of their land.

Besides it, there is no dispute raised by the respondents that as a result of present acquisition proceedings, the land owned by Lal Chand stood bifurcated as some part of it came on the other side of the minor.

In such circumstances, land owner-Lal Chand was required to be suitably compensated de-hors the construction of bridges existing over the old water course, especially when no evidence was produced on record by the respondents about any such construction near the left over of Lal Chand.

12. As such, in the totality of facts and circumstances of the present case, the award passed by the Reference Court is modified to the following effect:-
(i) in addition to the compensation-market value awarded by the Reference Court,
appellants/land owners shall be entitled to all statutory benefits and interest as contemplated under Section 23(2) 23(1-A) read with Section 34 of the 1894 Act.
(ii) land owner-Lal Chand shall also be entitled for 20% of the market value against severance of his land on account of construction of Dhundheri minor from R.D. 0 to 34750 off taking from RD 114840 Sirsa branch.
13
Accordingly, the aforementioned appeals stand disposed of in the aforesaid terms.
14. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
